dates.title: Wentworth - How to Apply for Undergraduate Admissions (deadlines, test policy)

fy.title: Wentworth - First Year Students (when to apply)

test_policy.notes: Test-optional since 2018. International students need not submit SAT/ACT but must prove English proficiency. Merit scholarship eligibility does not depend on submitting scores. Home-schooled applicants and applicants from schools with narrative assessments instead of 4.0 grades are excluded from the test-optional policy.

requirements.notes: Common Application or the Wentworth application; $50 fee (waivable for financial need per CDS). Applicants apply to a specific major. Official transcript sent directly from the school (Naviance/Parchment accepted); up to two recommendation letters are optional; no portfolio required for first-year applicants, including architecture and design majors. Prerequisites: four years of English, Algebra II and one lab science (CDS: 9 required units). Optional one-on-one interview for international applicants. A bank letter showing funds of USD $71,382 is required for the I-20, not for admission.

deadlines.label: Early Decision, fall 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Notification by early December; enrollment deposit by May 1. The 2025-26 Common Data Set answered No to an early decision plan, but the current admissions pages list this round. The pages give no year, so fall 2027 entry is assumed.

deadlines.label: Early Action round 1
deadlines.notes: Notified by mid-December. Early application scholarship ($2,000) is awarded to students applying by ED (Nov 1), EA1 (Nov 15) or EA2 (Jan 1). No year is printed, so fall 2027 entry is assumed.

deadlines.label: Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: Notified by April 1; enroll by May 1. The international undergraduate page lists no separate international deadlines, so the first-year dates apply.

deadlines.label: International need-based aid application: ED, EA1, EA2 applicants
deadlines.notes: Must be submitted before the admission decision. Limited International Grant for admitted international students.

deadlines.label: International need-based aid application: Regular Decision applicants

english_policy.waiver_notes: Exempt: secondary education in a listed English-speaking country (or a bachelor's degree from one); 3+ years of college-prep English at an English-language high school; C or higher in English I and II at a U.S. college; SAT EBRW 525+ (code 3958) or ACT reading 18 and English 20 (code 1928). Intensive English alternative: completion of listed ESL levels (Approach ISC B2, ASC English Level 5, BU CELOP, EF, ELS, FLS) with a letter from the center director or teacher. TOEFL, IELTS and DET scores are valid for two years.

english.notes: Tests taken on or before Jan 20, 2026; no subsection below 17. ETS code 3958.
Tests taken on or after Jan 21, 2026; page prints 4 with no subsection lower than 4 without naming the scale (it is the 1-6 scale).

aid.notes: International students are considered for merit scholarships based on secondary-school results; the Presidential Merit Scholarship (tuition, renewable 8 semesters) averages $20,000-$25,000 for Wentworth students generally (page not specific to international students). Starting with fall 2026 applicants a limited number of need-based International Grants are offered; the need-based aid application must be filed before the admission decision. From the Common Data Set: 158 nonresidents received institutional aid, average $9,677.

majors.program: Engineering (aerospace, biomedical, civil, computer, electrical, mechanical and others)
majors.notes: Applicants apply to a specific major. Precalculus is not required, but some programs (applied mathematics, computer science, cybersecurity, data science, engineering) may require a summer course to complete the math sequence.

majors.program: Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Data Science and Applied AI
majors.notes: Applicants apply to a specific major; some may require a summer math course (see engineering note).

majors.program: Architecture, Interior Design and Industrial Design
majors.notes: No portfolio is required for first-year applicants (required only for transfers seeking design/drawing credit).
Applicants apply to a specific major; no extra admission requirements stated.

sat.note: Wentworth school code (also its TOEFL code).

toefl.note: ETS school code; send scores directly via ETS.

ielts.note: No institution code is listed; official results must be sent to the school.

tier_notes.general: Our estimate: an 88% admit rate (76% for international applicants) and a 1300 SAT median among the 22% who submit place Wentworth just above the open-access D tier.
tier_notes.engineering: Our estimate: a technical institute in Boston with ABET-accredited engineering programs; no ranking cited. Placed in the 41-100 range for undergraduate engineering.
tier_notes.arts_design: Our estimate: accredited architecture, interior and industrial design programs; no ranking cited.
